summary.gateRReason: SC-94.1 requires that the site never carry a statement about itself that its own code contradicts. Five statements are contradicted: SC-01c ('and none on a phone' — a WebGL canvas mounts on iPhone 13 and Pixel 5), SC-08 (the prompt-reconstruction-engine Limits line — an automated benchmark exists with committed results), SC-09 (the jyotish-shastra Limits line — the repository ships a large interpretation and report-synthesis layer), SC-23 (MiniVic's 'no server to maintain' — two Cloud Functions are wired and /api/chat answers), and SC-26 (the sitemap's monthly change frequency). Three of the five are in visitor-visible copy. Separately, R-182's deploy-time refresh is not implemented (harvest_repos.mjs is not in build:static) and R-183's first-party instrumentation is not built, so neither of those two requirements is satisfiable by copy alone.

verification: Read components/gl/Scene.tsx: the render gate is `const show = capability === 'supported' && allowMotion && near && pageSettled;` (line 91). capability comes from components/gl/useGLCapability.ts, which tests only for a WebGL2/WebGL context and a non-software renderer. components/sections/Hero/HeroAtmosphere.tsx:50 — `material.uniforms.uQuality.value = size.width >= 900 ? 1 : 0;` with a comment at lines 31-34 explaining that below phone width the ridged near layer and the shafts are dropped. This is a designed-in phone rendering path, i.e. the code expects the scene to run on a phone.
Playwright trace at https://forgotten-mistory.web.app/?gl=force on devices['iPhone 13'] (390 px) and devices['Pixel 5'] (393 px), instrumenting getContext and sampling live canvases.
claims.observed: On iPhone 13 (innerWidth 390) a live WebGL canvas mounted inside #hero (622x888) and later inside #experience (622x888). On Pixel 5 (innerWidth 393): #hero 687x1717, then #experience 627x888. Identical behaviour to desktop. The ?gl=force parameter suppresses only the software-rasteriser rejection in useGLCapability.ts:40-42 — it touches no viewport or device logic — so it faithfully models a real phone with a working GPU, which is precisely the device this claim is about. On the unmodified URL in headless Chrome the renderer is classified as software and only the throwaway probe context is created, which is why a default trace shows one webgl2 getContext call and zero canvases; that is the fallback path, not the phone path.
claims.severity: high — this is visitor-visible copy in the site's own colophon, in the same sentence as the telemetry claim, on a page whose entire argument is that its statements can be checked

Choose one and ship both halves in one deployment: (a) ADD the gate — give Scene.tsx a real phone gate (e.g. `window.matchMedia('(max-width: 899px)')` or a coarse-pointer test) so no context is created below the width HeroAtmosphere already treats as a phone, remove the now-dead uQuality===0 branch in HeroAtmosphere.tsx:50 and atmosphere.glsl.ts:127 as a shipped removal under R-162, and keep the sentence as written; or (b) FIX the sentence — rewrite the colophon to what the code does, e.g. 'at most one WebGL context per section, and a reduced shader on a phone', and keep the phone path. Option (b) is cheaper and matches the deliberate engineering already in HeroAtmosphere; option (a) is the stronger performance stance. Either way the colophon and Scene.tsx must be changed in the same commit.

claims.verbatim: It's deployed as a static export on Firebase — no server to maintain. | ... so there's no server to run and no invented claims. | No backend, no hallucination surface beyond the fact base.
claims.context: MiniVic's own answers about this site — statements the site makes about itself, delivered to a visitor in conversation.
verification: Read firebase.json hosting.rewrites.
curl -X POST https://forgotten-mistory.web.app/api/chat -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"message":"hi"}'
curl -i GET https://forgotten-mistory.web.app/api/chat
curl -X POST https://forgotten-mistory.web.app/api/tts
Read functions/index.js and lib/miniVicBrain.ts:317-360.
claims.observed: There IS a server. firebase.json declares two Cloud Function rewrites: /api/chat -> minivicChat (us-central1) and /api/tts -> elevenLabsTts (us-central1). In production POST /api/chat returns HTTP 400 with the JSON body {"error":"messages_required"} — the function executed and validated the request body — and GET /api/chat returns HTTP 405 application/json. A pure static host would have returned the SPA HTML. functions/index.js proxies OpenRouter with a server-side key. lib/miniVicBrain.ts:315-322 documents this openly in a code comment ('the same-origin /api/chat function (a Firebase Function via Hosting rewrite ...). The OpenRouter key stays server-side.'), so the codebase knows what the chatbot denies. POST /api/tts returns HTTP 502, i.e. reachable and failing, not absent. Separately, the shipped bundle inlines a referrer-locked public Gemini key (out/_next/static/chunks/app/layout-*.js contains a generativelanguage reference; next.config.js:6 documents the restriction) and the deployed CSP permits connect-src to generativelanguage.googleapis.com and *.googleapis.com — so a visitor who uses MiniVic sends their typed question to Google and/or through the Cloud Function to OpenRouter.
claims.severity: high — the contradiction is between the site's spoken self-description and its own deployment configuration, which is exactly the failure mode R-183 names
claims.remediation: Rewrite all three answers in app/data/miniVicKnowledge.ts (723, 726, 728) to describe the deployment that exists: a Next.js static export on Firebase Hosting, plus two Cloud Functions behind same-origin rewrites — minivicChat, which proxies OpenRouter with a server-side key, and elevenLabsTts — with a browser-side Gemini tier behind a referrer-locked public key and a deterministic offline keyword fallback over the same typed fact base. State plainly that a question asked of MiniVic leaves the browser. Then reconcile the two stale code comments at components/MiniVicBot.tsx:832 ('No server-side cloned-voice TTS is provisioned on this deployment' — /api/tts answers 502, so it is provisioned and broken; either fix it or de-provision the rewrite) and components/MiniVicBot.tsx:1061 ('Static deployments have no /api routes' — this one does). This claim and SC-01a must be rewritten in the SAME deployment, because the honest telemetry statement has to name this third-party flow.
